subtitle: "REST API, token login, general export job, cached locally"

```{mermaid}
%%| file: diagrams/obis.mmd
```

## What this does

EcoTaxa's REST API (`{ECOTAXA_URL}/api/docs`) exposes a **general export** job: it writes a zip with one TSV
per sample (object, sample, acquisition and process fields, plus each object's category, annotation status,
annotator and date) and, optionally, the images. This notebook logs in with a token, starts the job for
the project, waits for it, downloads and unzips it under `data/export/`, and reads the TSVs into one objects
table cached as Parquet. Later notebooks read the cache and never touch the node.

The project is `ECOTAXA_PROJECT_ID` (default 2, the demo project; the setup below prints which one this
page ran on). Credentials come from a git-ignored `.Renviron` (`ECOTAXA_URL`, `ECOTAXA_USER`,
`ECOTAXA_PASSWORD`) or from `ECOTAXA_TOKEN`, a login token handed to the render so no password sits on the
machine. An export already unzipped under `data/export/` is reused unless `ECOTAXA_REFRESH=1`. When
no login is configured on project 2, the notebook falls back to the upstream test set in `data-raw/import_test/`, which is
the byte-identical source of project 2's eight objects (see `data-raw/README.md`), so the rest of the
pipeline still runs on the same data; it says so below.

```{r}
#| label: setup
librarian::shelf(httr2, dplyr, readr, tibble, arrow, jsonlite, here, quiet = TRUE)
for (f in list.files(here("R"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
PROJECT_ID <- ecotaxa_project_id()
cat("project", PROJECT_ID, "on", ecotaxa_url(), "\n")
DIR_EXPORT <- here("data/export", paste0("project-", PROJECT_ID))
dir.create(DIR_EXPORT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## The node, as anyone can see it

The project list, the instruments and the per-project taxonomy statistics are readable without a login on
this node; object data are not.

```{r}
#| label: public
projects <- ecotaxa_projects()
projects |> select(projid, title, instrument, instrument_url, objcount, pctvalidated, pctclassified)
stats <- ecotaxa_project_taxo_stats(PROJECT_ID)
str(stats)
```

## Export

```{r}
#| label: export
prior <- file.path(DIR_EXPORT, "export.json")
reuse <- file.exists(prior) && !identical(Sys.getenv("ECOTAXA_REFRESH"), "1") &&
  grepl("^EcoTaxa API", fromJSON(prior)$source) && length(ecotaxa_export_tsvs(DIR_EXPORT)) > 0
if (reuse) {
  tsv_paths <- ecotaxa_export_tsvs(DIR_EXPORT)
  source_of_objects <- fromJSON(prior)$source
  cat("reusing the export of", fromJSON(prior)$exported_utc, "(set ECOTAXA_REFRESH=1 to export again)\n")
} else if (ecotaxa_has_login()) {
  token <- ecotaxa_login()
  # a project of a million objects with images takes the node well over the default ten minutes
  tsv_paths <- ecotaxa_export(PROJECT_ID, DIR_EXPORT, token = token, with_images = "first", timeout_s = 6 * 3600)
  source_of_objects <- "EcoTaxa API general export"
} else {
  stopifnot("without a login only project 2 has a local fallback" = PROJECT_ID == 2L)
  tsv_paths <- list.files(here("data-raw/import_test"), pattern = "\\.tsv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  source_of_objects <- "data-raw/import_test (upstream test set; no ECOTAXA_USER/ECOTAXA_PASSWORD in this session)"
}
cat("objects come from:", source_of_objects, "\n")
cat(length(tsv_paths), "TSV files:", head(basename(tsv_paths), 5), if (length(tsv_paths) > 5) "...", "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: read
objects <- read_ecotaxa_export(tsv_paths)
# a general export without internal ids has the category's display name but not its id: resolve the
# id from the project's own categories, where each display name is unique
if (!"object_annotation_category_id" %in% names(objects)) {
  cats <- ecotaxa_taxa(stats$used_taxa)
  objects$object_annotation_category_id <- ecotaxa_category_ids(objects$object_annotation_category, cats)
  cat("category ids resolved from", nrow(cats), "project categories\n")
}
cat(nrow(objects), "objects,", n_distinct(objects$sample_id), "samples,",
    n_distinct(objects$acq_id), "acquisitions,", ncol(objects), "columns\n")
objects |> count(object_annotation_status)
# the most common categories (the whole table for a small project)
objects |>
  count(object_annotation_category, object_annotation_category_id, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(25)
```

## Cache

```{r}
#| label: cache
write_parquet(objects, file.path(DIR_EXPORT, "objects.parquet"))
from_api <- grepl("^EcoTaxa API", source_of_objects)
exported <- if (reuse) fromJSON(prior)$exported_utc else format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")
writeLines(toJSON(list(project_id = PROJECT_ID, source = source_of_objects, tsv = basename(tsv_paths),
                       n_objects = nrow(objects), exported_utc = exported,
                       image_dir = if (from_api) DIR_EXPORT else here("data-raw/import_test")),
                  auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), file.path(DIR_EXPORT, "export.json"))
files <- list.files(DIR_EXPORT, recursive = TRUE)
cat(length(files), "files;", sum(grepl("\\.(jpg|jpeg|png)$", files, ignore.case = TRUE)), "images\n")
```

## Notes

- The export carries `object_annotation_category_id`, the node's internal taxonomy id, which notebook 02 resolves.
  It carries no AphiaID.
- A login token from `POST /api/login` is a JWT; the API also offers `/token` with a refresh token, which a
  scheduled pipeline should prefer.
- `with_images = "first"` ships the visible image per object; `"all"` can produce several TSV lines per object.

## Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)

The first real export, of 967,734 objects, found five things the eight-object demo could not. Each is now
handled in `R/ecotaxa_api.R` or `R/taxa.R`, with a test:

| What happened | Cause | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` on starting the job | `split_by = ""` is not in the node's enum (`sample`, `acquisition`, `taxon`, `none`) | `ecotaxa_export_body()` checks against the OpenAPI enums |
| `500`, `relation "taxo_recast" does not exist` | the node's DB was built without two tables (a node issue, not a pipeline one) | fixed on the node; see [05 Migrate](05_migrate_from-ifremer.qmd) |
| the job sat at "1 % Start TSV export" forever | the back end was OOM-killed (2.44 GB container) loading every row at once; the job row is never updated after that | one job per batch of samples, at most `max_objects` (40,000) each; a job whose progress stalls for 20 min stops the run |
| `object_annotation_category_id` missing | the export carries internal ids only with `with_internal_ids` | the id is resolved from the category's display name (unique on a node) against the project's own categories; no match stops |
| every date blank downstream | the export writes `YYYY-MM-DD` and `HH:MM:SS`, the import format is `YYYYMMDD` and `HHMMSS` | `ecotaxa_datetime()` reads both |

Also: download with a long timeout and unzip with the system `unzip` (zip64, over 4 GB); batches leave a
marker under `data/export/project-<id>/batches/`, so a stopped run resumes after the last finished batch;
each finished job is deleted on the node so its files do not fill the node's disk. For project 4 the 28
batches took 44 minutes and gave 105 TSVs and exactly one image per object (967,734), which also removed the
6,962 byte-identical second images the backup carried.
